ratingScale.not-reported: not established from the primary source reviewed

interpretation: Ratings describe reported scope, not paper quality. Absence is not inferred when the primary source does not establish it.

works.title: Can Agent Benchmarks Support Their Scores? Evidence-Supported Bounds for Interactive-Agent Evaluation
works.primaryObject: Locked outcome-evidence checklists and Evidence Pass, Evidence Fail, or Unknown bounds for existing benchmarks
works.relationToP26002: Direct collision on locked evidence requirements, explicit missing evidence, and auditing whether benchmark scores are supported. P26-002 must not claim these concepts as new.

works.title: Toward Pre-Deployment Assurance for Enterprise AI Agents: Ontology-Grounded Simulation and Trust Certification
works.primaryObject: Operational envelopes, ontology-grounded scenarios, and a signed Trust Certificate used as a deployment gate
works.relationToP26002: Strong collision on pre-deployment testing, scenario-bound certification, coverage reporting, and cryptographic binding. Its semantic verdicts use LLM judges, leaving room for a deterministic-evaluator error study.

works.title: Governing Dynamic Capabilities: Cryptographic Binding and Reproducibility Verification for AI Agent Tool Use
works.primaryObject: Capability-bound certificates, reproducibility verification, and tamper-evident interaction ledgers
works.relationToP26002: The strongest cryptographic collision. It already evaluates Ed25519, SHA-256, hash chains, attacks, false positives, baselines, and overhead. P26-002 must treat its cryptography as an experimental treatment, not a primitive contribution.

works.title: AgentBound: Verifiable Behavioral Governance for Autonomous AI Agents
works.primaryObject: Signed governance receipts with external reconstruction and deterministic policy-decision replay
works.relationToP26002: Direct collision on portable verification, policy provenance, signatures, replay, and tamper-evident audit records. Its scope is runtime governance rather than comparative evaluator measurement.

works.title: AgentReputation: A Decentralized Agentic AI Reputation Framework
works.primaryObject: Evidence-based, context-conditioned reputation cards and verification-strength metadata
works.relationToP26002: Relevant to downstream use of verified trials and context-specific claims, but presented as an architectural vision rather than an empirical evaluator benchmark.

works.title: When Agentic Executions Fail: Detecting and Localizing Runtime Faults from Telemetry
works.primaryObject: Detection and localization of ten injected operational fault types from 275 sanitized, aligned agent-execution traces
works.relationToP26002: The strongest new collision on runtime-fault benchmarks, aligned no-fault controls, telemetry diagnosis, and localization. P26-002 cannot claim novelty for fault detection or localization. Its remaining question is narrower: accept/reject evaluator error under precommitted evidence contracts and portable integrity checks, not top-k fault diagnosis.

works.title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
works.primaryObject: Utility and security evaluation under indirect prompt injection in realistic tool environments
works.relationToP26002: Provides an established environment and attack family for independent external validation. P26-002 should reuse or adapt it instead of claiming prompt-injection scenarios as new.

works.title: Identifying the Risks of LM Agents with an LM-Emulated Sandbox
works.primaryObject: Adversarial scenario generation and an LLM-emulated sandbox for high-stakes tool-use risk
works.relationToP26002: Established prior art for scalable adversarial agent trials. Its LLM emulator and evaluator make it useful as a baseline or external target, not a zero-cost deterministic core.

works.title: AgentRewardBench: Evaluating Automatic Evaluations of Web Agent Trajectories
works.primaryObject: Meta-evaluation of LLM judges against expert labels for web-agent success, side effects, and repetition
works.relationToP26002: Direct collision on meta-evaluating agent evaluators. P26-002 must differentiate through claim-specific contracts, controlled fault and control pairs, deterministic checks, and portable integrity evidence.

works.title: AgentAtlas: Beyond Outcome Leaderboards for LLM Agents
works.primaryObject: Control-decision and trajectory-failure taxonomies plus a benchmark-coverage audit
works.relationToP26002: Constrains taxonomy novelty and supplies coverage axes. P26-002 should map its eight families to this vocabulary and keep its synthetic pilot out of efficacy claims.

works.title: tau-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
works.primaryObject: Database-state outcome evaluation, domain-policy compliance, and repeat reliability through pass^k
works.relationToP26002: Established prior art for repeated reliability and environment-state checks. It is a candidate external target for testing whether portable evidence changes evaluator error.

works.title: Success Is Not Self-Explanatory: Auditing Success Provenance in Agent Evaluation
works.primaryObject: Within-unit CLEAN, GOLD, and SHAM interventions that test whether success follows acquired target information
works.relationToP26002: Strong collision on matched provenance interventions and paired analysis. P26-002 should use matched controls and position itself around evaluator false acceptance under evidence contracts, not provenance as a new object.

works.title: Progent: Programmable Privilege Control for LLM Agents
works.primaryObject: Deterministic, argument-level tool policies for runtime privilege control
works.relationToP26002: Established prior art for deterministic scope enforcement. P26-002 may evaluate permission faults but cannot claim programmable privilege control as a contribution.
